description: Audit given Kotlin class(es)/file(s)/package scope in a Kotlin Multiplatform (Android + iOS) project for complete KDoc coverage across every source set — `commonMain`, `androidMain`, `iosMain`/`appleMain`/`nativeMain` (and `jvmMain` when present) of the shared module plus the Android app module's sources — with the KMP rule that an `expect` declaration carries the KDoc and its `actual`s inherit it (an `actual` gets its own KDoc only for genuinely platform-specific behavior), while platform-only public API (an `iosMain`-only helper, Compose `MainViewController()`, an `androidMain`-only extension) is documented where it lives. Checks type-level docs, `@property`/`@param`/ `@constructor`, every function/property within the discovered visibility bar, enum entries, companion and nested declarations, `@return`/`@throws`/`@see`/`@sample`, `@suppress` honored, and the Dokka `module.md` (`# Module` / `# Package` sections) wired via `includes.from(...)` for every module/package touched (creating them if missing); generates any missing or incomplete KDoc grounded in the actual code and current changes, then runs the module's Dokka 2 multiplatform build (`dokkaGeneratePublicationHtml`, else `dokkaGenerate`; Dokka 1 `dokkaHtml` fallback) to confirm the KDoc is well-formed and reports its warnings — unresolved links per source set and, when the project enables `reportUndocumented`, `Undocumented:` lines tagged `(common)`/`(android)`/`(ios)`. Invoke as `/iru-kmp-dokka <scope>` where `<scope>` is a comma-separated list of class names, file paths, or a package glob, or `/iru-kmp-dokka` with no argument to scope to Kotlin files touched by uncommitted changes plus commits on the current branch not yet on the base branch. Swift code in `iosApp/` is out of scope (see `iru-swift-docc`). Discovers the project's own documentation bar (detekt `comments` rules, Dokka `documentedVisibilities`/`reportUndocumented`, contributor guides, observed practice) rather than assuming a fixed style. Equivalent to `iru-android-dokka`/ `iru-kotlin-kdoc` for KMP apps. Use whenever the user (or `iru-kmp-code-one-task-group` via `iru-gate-runner`) wants KDoc completeness checked and filled in for KMP code, instead of relying on a Dokka run (which doesn't fail on undocumented members by default) to surface gaps.
